calls.title: Growthbook <> Picnic - POC Scoping/Kickoff
calls.summary: The meeting outlined a three-week proof of concept (POC) for integrating GrowthBook into Picnic's operations, beginning with integration tasks in the first week, followed by conducting an experiment in the second week and reviewing results in the final week. The goals include validating the connection between GrowthBook and Picnic's data infrastructure, enhancing the ease of running experiments, and considering feature flag evaluations later. Resource allocation will involve 1-2 weeks of effort from developers and analysts with minimal disruption to ongoing projects. The importance of security reviews was highlighted, with a checklist provided by GrowthBook to clarify requirements. Additionally, the POC will be free of charge, with deployment options discussed, favoring a cloud-managed setup.

calls.summary: The team outlined their plan to initiate the proof of concept (POC) starting in week 28, specifically July 6th, following a necessary security review and completion of current roadmap tasks. They will provide early access to SDK documentation and account provisioning to facilitate a soft start before the formal POC launch. A security review is in progress, with no current issues reported regarding vendor integration. The team plans to conduct several experiments, including one high-impact test and a new live test in the second week of the POC with established success metrics. They are also addressing team availability, noting upcoming time off and supporting asynchronous coordination, with European engineering resources available. A proactive approach to communication and documentation sharing is in place, fostering collaboration and project transparency.

calls.summary: The team confirmed their readiness to advance with the proof of concept (PoC), primarily focusing on backend SDK integration led by Danilo and a recipe search experiment comparing keyword versus hybrid approaches. Dan Wathne ensured account setup is underway, while communication channels were established for support during the PoC. Privacy concerns were addressed, confirming that no data would leave Picnic NL's systems, only aggregated data would be used, aligning with security requirements. A pricing overview meeting is scheduled to clarify commercial expectations, while clear support roles from Natasha and August were defined to ensure timely responses throughout the process. Overall, the discussion highlighted a collaborative effort towards a successful evaluation with structured processes in place.

calls.title: Growthbook <> Picnic - Pricing Sync
calls.summary: The meeting focused on the nearly completed backend integration and experiment setup, which is currently hindered by the need for privacy confirmation and Snowflake connection. The internal data analysts are responsible for metric definitions, with emphasis on aligning metrics to avoid inconsistencies. Quality versus quantity in experimentation was deliberated, with a need for standardized methods to ensure actionable results. A pricing model was introduced, indicating an estimated cost for 50-100 seats, alongside a flexible proposal to start with fewer seats at a discounted rate. The teams agreed on the necessity of continuous collaboration and expert guidance to refine experimentation practices and develop a robust business case for scaling usage.

calls.title: Growthbook <> Picnic - Experimentation Best Practice Session
calls.summary: Participants discussed the importance of aligning experimentation goals with strategic metrics to enhance the quality of insights derived from experiments. Misaligned experiments currently lead to inconclusive results, wasting resources and causing decision fatigue. Stefan highlighted the need for standardized customer journey metrics to better understand customer behavior across stages. Luke emphasized the significance of coordinated team metrics to prevent cannibalization and facilitate faster learning. The discussion also covered offline and online experimentation, advocating for offline validation as a quality gate. GrowthBook's capabilities were reviewed, noting its support for metric standardization and the limitations in guiding decisions beyond basic outcomes. Overall, the conversation aimed to enhance organizational alignment and cultivate a culture that maximizes the value of experimentation.
calls.keywords: Experimentation, Metrics, Offline Evaluation, Online Testing, GrowthBook, Customer Journeys
